questions.text: Which one of the following well-formed formulae in predicate calculus is NOT valid?
questions.solution:
Option 4 is not valid: take a domain {1, 2} with p(1), q(2) true and p(2), q(1) false. Then every x satisfies p(x) [latex]\vee[/latex] q(x), but neither "all p" nor "all q" holds.

Options 1-3 are standard valid implications.

Answer: Option 4

questions.text: Suppose that the eigen values of matrix A are 1, 2, 4. The determinant of [latex](A^{-1})^{T}[/latex] is _________.
questions.solution:
[latex]\det A=1\times2\times4=8[/latex]. Transpose does not change the determinant, and [latex]\det(A^{-1})=\frac{1}{\det A}[/latex].

[latex]\det(A^{-1})^T=\frac18=0.125[/latex]

Answer: 0.125

questions.text:
Consider the systems,each consisting of m linear equations in n variables.
I. If m [latex]\lt[/latex] n, then all such systems have a solution
II. If m [latex]\gt[/latex] n, then none of these systems has a solution
III. If m = n, then there exists a system which has a solution
Which one of the following is CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: m [latex]\lt[/latex] n does not guarantee a solution: x + y = 1 and x + y = 2 are inconsistent [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: m [latex]\gt[/latex] n systems can have solutions (e.g. the same equation repeated) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- III: with m = n, the homogeneous system Ax = 0 always has x = 0 as a solution [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Only III is true

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: I, II and III are true
Only II and III are true

questions.text: Let f(x) be a polynomial and g(x) = f'(x) be its derivative. If the degree of (f(x)+ f(-x)) is 10, then the degree of (g(x)-g(-x)) is ________.
questions.solution:
[latex]f(x)+f(-x)[/latex] keeps only the even powers of f (times 2). Its degree is 10, so f has an [latex]x^{10}[/latex] term (and no higher even power).

[latex]g(x)-g(-x)[/latex] keeps only the odd powers of g = f'. Even powers of f become odd powers of g: [latex]x^{10}\rightarrow10x^9[/latex] is the highest.

Degree = 9

Answer: 9

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

[latex](x^3+x^4+\cdots)^3=x^9(1+x+x^2+\cdots)^3=x^9(1-x)^{-3}[/latex]

We need the coefficient of [latex]x^3[/latex] in [latex](1-x)^{-3}[/latex]: [latex]\binom{3+2}{2}=10[/latex].

Answer: 10
